title: Robots Versus Wrestlers
cn: 第 22 集 · 机器人对阵摔跤手
novel:
Ted threw his annual party, and this year's theme was "[[Robots|robot]] Versus [[Wrestlers|wrestler]]." Half the guests came as machines, half as muscled fighters, and the two sides [[clashed|clash]] on the dance floor.

A deeper [[debate|debate]] raged in the kitchen. Was [[high culture|high culture]] — opera, poetry, fine wine — better than [[low culture|low culture]]? Or was a good wrestling match just as [[valid|valid]] as a symphony?

Ted argued for the [[intellectual|intellectual]] side. Marshall, wearing a robot helmet, [[defended|defend]] the joy of simple things. Robin said both were [[ridiculous|ridiculous]]. Barney, in a tuxedo, declared that suits [[transcended|transcend]] all culture.

Lily watched the [[chaos|chaos]] and laughed. "Why does it have to be one or the other?" she said. "A person can love Shakespeare and a [[flashy|flashy]] robot fight."

The room fell quiet. She was right, of course. The best evenings, Ted realized, held both — the [[sophisticated|sophisticated]] and the silly, the [[profound|profound]] and the [[absurd|absurd]], all dancing together under the same roof.

robot.en: a machine that can move and do tasks

wrestler.en: a person who fights in a wrestling match

clash.en: to fight or argue against another side

debate.en: a discussion where people argue sides

high culture.en: art and ideas valued as refined

valid.en: fair and based on good reasons

defend.en: to speak in support of something

flashy.en: big and bright to attract attention
